summary: Alfred Cort Haddon worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at King's College London (~1871–1874) and Christ's College (~1875–1879), later holding posts at the University of Cambridge (1879–1880, 1900–1926) and the Royal College of Science for Ireland (1880–1901).

Alfred Edward Housman studied at Bromsgrove School, King Edward's School, Birmingham (~1871–1872), and St John's College, Oxford (~1877–1881). He held a post at University College London from circa 1892 to 1911.

Alfred Ernout was a linguist. He held academic posts at the University of Lille (1913–1924), the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1913–1951), the University of Paris (~1927–1944), and the Collège de France (1941–1951).

Alfred Forke specialized in Sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Geneva and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1886–1889). He later served at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen zu Berlin (1903–1923) and the University of Hamburg (~1923–1935).

Alfred Foucher worked in Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Sylvain Lévi at the EPHE. His posts included the EFEO (director 1905), EPHE, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and University of Paris (professor 1929–1936).

Alfred Gell studied at Cambridge (~1963–1967) under Edmund Leach and completed a Ph.D. at the London School of Economics (~1967–1972). He held posts at the University of Sussex (~1971–1974), Australian National University (1974), and LSE (1979).

Alfred Hillebrandt worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his doctorate at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler (~1871–1875) and studied under Martin Haug at Munich (~1875–1876). He held a chair at Breslau from 1887 to 1921.

Alfred Körte specialized in history, archaeology, and linguistics, studying at the University of Bonn (~1885–1890). He held posts at Bonn, Greifswald, Basel, Giessen, Freiburg, and Leipzig University (~1917–1934).

Alfred Ludwig was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Vienna and Berlin under Albrecht Weber, Moriz Haupt, August Boeckh, and others. He held a post in Vienna (1858) and served as professor at Charles University (1860–1871).

Alfred Radcliffe-Brown studied at King Edward's School, Birmingham, and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1901–1906). He held posts at the University of Sydney (~1925–1931), University of Chicago (~1931–1937), University of Oxford (~1937–1946), and FESP in São Paulo (~1942–1944).

Linguist Alice Harris studied at the University of Massachusetts Amherst and Harvard University (~1970–1976). She held faculty posts at Vanderbilt University (~1979–2009) and the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~2009).

Alicia Turner specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, where she was supervised by Bruce Lincoln and Steven Collins, and studied under Saw Tun, Daw Than Than Win, John Okell, and Carol S. Anderson.

Alison Denton Jones is a scholar in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She was supervised for her doctorate by Martin King Whyte and also studied under Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret Dornish.

Alka Patel specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Mount Holyoke College (~1985–1989) and earned her PhD from Harvard University (~1991–2000). Around 2007, she held an associate professorship at the University of California, Irvine.

Allan G. Grapard worked in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, earning a Ph.D. from INALCO. He held posts as ISF Professor of Shinto Studies (~1985–2004) and Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultural Studies at UC Santa Barbara.

Allan Gibbard is a philosopher who studied at Swarthmore College (~1959–1963) and Harvard University (~1965–1971). He held positions at the University of Chicago (1969–1974), the University of Pittsburgh (1974–1977), and the University of Michigan (1977–2016).
Allan H. Barr is a Sinologist who earned his doctorate from the University of Oxford by 1983. He held an attested post in 2001 as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College.

Indologist Allen Wright Thrasher completed his doctoral studies under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1968–1972) and studied with traditional teachers V. B. Deo, R. S. Raghavachariar, and K. A. Sivaramakrishna Sastri. He served at the Library of Congress (~1985–2013).
Alnis Dickson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at McGill University (attested 2009) under supervisor Lara Braitstein, and also studied under G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Alois Anton Führer studied at Würzburg (PhD 1874–1879) and with Georg Bühler. He held posts at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1881–1884), Lucknow State Museum (1884–1899), Archaeological Survey of India (~1885–1898), and the Christian Catholic Church of Switzerland (1906–1930).
